sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Dung Eater** is an character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A self-described "scourge upon the living," the loathesome Dung Eater is a Tarnished who revels in murder and defilement. He places the Seedbed Curse on his victims to sever their souls from the Erdtree and its grace, trapping them in eternal torment.

The Dung Eater has the heart of an Omen without the body to match. He wears a malformed set of hefty red armor with tufts of red hair emerging from the bleeding stumps of its severed Omen horns. His helmet has no opening except for a deep gash over the right eye. His heavy, sun-shaped medallion represents the guidance he once saw, and the ring to which it will one day lead. He wields an accursed sword forged from the saw-like spine of the shrieking, malformed giant Milos, whose perceived deformity mirrored his own. This is his ideal form, and a reflection of the landscape of his mind.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Dung Eater envisioned an Order that would place a "pox upon life itself." He murdered and defiled countless victims in a reviled ritual that produced Seedbed Curses, severing the dead souls from the Erdtree and binding them to his own flesh. Those cursed in this way were doomed to be reborn as Omen, passing the curse to their descendants for all eternity. With each pox, the Dung Eater nourished and grew his own Seedbed Curse. He personally cultivated thousands of these horn-strewn tumors across the realm. The art was among the most vile things in the entire Lands Between.

The Dung Eater was caught and imprisoned for his unspeakable crimes, but his work continued unperturbed, much to the horror of fellow inmate Blackguard Big Boggart. Then, he was publicly hanged in front of an angry crowd beneath the sun. Upon his death, the Dung Eater received Queen Marika's grace. The Dung Eater visited Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, the Volcano Manor and Leyndell, Royal Capital after his revival. He was jailed with the noble Omen in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and eventually lost sight of his guiding grace.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown:
The Dung Eater's red phantom appears at the Roundtable Hold when the Tarnished reaches the Altus Plateau. He sits on the floor among a pile of bodies in the room adjacent to Sir Gideon Ofnir's study. Though he does not respect his fellow Tarnished, he abides by the pact of non-aggression. Roderika, Spirit Tuner senses the spirits trapped by the Dung Eater and warns the Tarnished of the curse.

If the player collects a Seedbed Curse and speaks to the Dung Eater, the Dung Eater detects its presence. He produces a Sewer-Gaol Key and asks the Tarnished to release his corporeal body from the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds. If he is released, the Dung Eater attacks and defiles Blackguard Big Boggart. When the player discovers the evidence, the Dung Eater invades them as well. If repelled, Dung Eater exclaims something unexpected happened. Despite the curse stirring within, his blessing was warded off by the protagonist—a feat none had succeeded in before.

The Dung Eater has a revelation: he was not the one who could curse the world as in his vision. He was just the means to get there; his flesh is the one that must receive the blessing. He asks to be killed and defiled by the Seedbed Curse until his gestated Mending Rune of the Fell Curse coalesces. If this Rune is added to the Elden Ring, it curses Order itself and ushers in the Blessing of Despair.

The Tarnished may also choose to simply kill him, leave him in his jail, or turn him into a puppet with Seluvis's Potion.

sections.heading: Questline progression
sections.markdown:
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Laskyar Ruins)
 - Head north-west from the Site of Grace to find Rya the Scout inside a gazebo and talk to her.
 - Move to north-west again from here to find Blackguard Big Boggart at the Boilprawn Shack and talk to him: select **Give me the necklace** and then **Deal** to be able to buy Rya's Necklace from him for 1000 Runes.
 - After purchasing the item, he'll start selling an infinite supply of Boiled Prawns. Purchase at least one to progress his questline: you'll receive the "Spread Out" gesture and, in turn, Boggart's summon sign will appear at the Ruin-Strewn Precipice Overlook to aid you against Magma Wyrm Makar.
1. Roundtable Hold
 - After touching any Site of Grace in Altus Plateau, the Dung Eater will appear in the western quarter of the Roundtable Hold, past Gideon's study. Talk to him with at least one Seedbed Curse in inventory to receive the Sewer-Gaol Key.
 - *(Optional)* Talking to Roderika, she'll now have a new dialogue option "**There's something you should know**" to warn you of the danger of the new arrival.
1. Leyndell, Royal Capital (Underground Roadside)
 - Drop down the open grate to the left exiting the room and follow the path past the Miranda Flowers to reach the Dung Eater's cell, which is guarded by a Large Fingercreeper hidden underground and some smaller ones hanging from the ceiling. Open the cell and talk to him, selecting **Leave your gaol!**.
1. Leyndell, Royal Capital (Forsaken Depth)
 - *(Optional)* The Dung Eater can now be summoned to aid you against Mohg, the Omen.
1. Leyndell, Royal Capital (Queen's Bed Chamber)
 - *(Optional)* Alongside Melina, the Dung Eater can now be summoned to aid you against Morgott, the Omen King.
1. Roundtable Hold
 - *(Optional)* The Dung Eater has disappeared from the Hold, leaving behind on his spot a message that reads: "**I'll defile you next. Come to the outer moat.**"
 - *(Optional)* Talking to Roderika, she'll now have a new dialogue option "**About the spirits' voices**" to express her relief for the Dung Eater's departure.
1. Leyndell, Royal Capital (Outer Wall Battleground)
 - Visit the moat to the south-east below the capital's ramparts to meet again with Boggart, who now sells an infinite supply of Boiled Crabs too. Talk to him and select **About the Dung Eater**.
 - Reload the area to find Boggart moribund and, after talking to him, collect Seedbed Curse, Blackguard's Bell Bearing, Iron Ball, and Blackguard's Iron Mask from his cadaver. Shortly after, the Dung Eater will invade you and, once defeated, will drop his Sword of Milos.
1. Roundtable Hold
 - The Dung Eater will have now returned to the Hold. Talking to him, he'll instruct you to defile his corpse with the Seedbed Curse.
 - *(Optional)* Talking to Roderika, she'll now have a new dialogue option "**About the spirits' voices**".
1. Leyndell, Royal Capital (Underground Roadside)
 - (Optional) If you don't intend to follow his questline, you can select **Administer Seluvis' Potion** to turn the Dung Eater into a puppet. After his screams have ceased, you're free to kill him to collect his loot without failing the Preceptor's questline.
 - After collecting all five Seedbed Curses, return to him and select **Use the Seedbed Curse**, then collect the Mending Rune of the Fell Curse from his body. Reloading the area, you'll be able to collect the Omen Set too.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Roderika cautions the spiritual harm done by the Dung Eater's Seedbed Curse is worse than Godrick's grafting.
- The Dung Eater possesses a fate.
- During the intro cinematic, the Dung Eater is hung by an iron chain in a gallows, silhouetted against the bright Erdtree or sun. A faint golden Grace near his chest illuminates the sun medallion, visually linking it to the haloed backdrop.
- He was confined to the same prison as nobleborn Omen beneath the streets of Leyndell. Like the Omen, his body also contains cursed spirits.
- Two Seedbed Curses are found at Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, regardless of whether he is freed. This suggests he was among (or descended from) the Tarnished who remained in the Lands Between.
- The Dung Eater's right eye is visible through the gash in the Omen Helm in the Dung Eater concept art.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Like all human NPCs, the Dung Eater has a custom face. He has wild red hair and eyes that are spaced too widely apart, giving him an almost deformed appearance. He is the only character who looks this way.
 - The Fell God is described as being "malformed," and is also associated with giants, horns, red hair, and the sun. It was ousted by Queen Marika during the War Against the Giants.
 - Milos is also described as grotesque.
- The Dung Eater’s name and methods may draw inspiration from an old Japanese myth in which a person’s soul was believed to reside in a special organ located inside the anus. Known as the , this mythical sphere was said to be extracted by demons to steal their victim’s soul. The Dung Eater’s grotesque ritual may symbolically mirror this act, as he seizes the souls of his victims by defiling them to their core.
 - The Headless can steal the *shirikodama* in *Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice*. These enemies are physically similar to Omen, though they are bloated and hornless. Like the Dung Eater, they were previously executed for great crimes.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Finger Reader Crones** are a set of eight characters in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The eldery Finger Reader Crones were immortal oracles who divined messages from the Greater Will and its vassals, the Two Fingers, speaking on their behalf. They perceived the Fingers' formless language of light, interpreting their motions into speech. Finger Readers congregated in Leyndell, Royal Capital during the age of the Erdtree. One was rumored to have served as wet nurse to Godwyn the Golden.

When the Two Fingers atop the Divine Towers fell inert during or after the Shattering, many Finger Readers became dormant. Those who remained active continued to seek fingers to read.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The nameless Finger Reader Crones are **eight** stationary NPCs who offer hints at various checkpoints throughout the Lands Between. They are not tied to any quests and offer none of their own, so interacting with them is optional. The seated Finger Readers are eager to glean the fate of others from the wrinkles in their fingers. If the Tarnished approaches one of them, they become overly excited and beg to see their fingers, to read their future. They have the gift of foresight, offering vague and cryptic clues, usually about the area they reside in or a quest yet to be undertaken.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: Before Shattering the Elden Ring, Queen Marika sent her Demigod son on an unsung cleansing crusade against the land of the Tower, veiling both in a Realm of Shadow. It was to this land that Miquella the Kind departed, divesting himself of his flesh, his strength, his lineage, and of all things Golden. The Tarnished joins his followers, beckoned to trace the Empyrean's painful pilgrimage through a land scorched by Messmer's flame. Uncover the dark secrets of the Scadutree, and witness the birth of a new god at the heart of the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Elden Ring: The Road to the Erdtree** is a manga adaptation of Elden Ring. The artist and author, Nikiichi Tobita, decided to make the adaptation into a comedy with a main character named Aseo. The official website offers the first and last two chapters for free, with the ones in between disappearing to be later published physically.

The release date of the first physical volume in English was on May 23, 2023.

sections.heading: Full storyline
sections.markdown:
There was one other, a Tarnished of no renown. A wretch of Reedlandish descent, called by Grace, to cross the fog into the Lands Between, to stand before the Elden Ring and succeed Queen Marika, as the Elden Lord.

The Tarnished awoke in the Chapel of Anticipation. After a run in with the Grafted Scion, he ended up in the Stranded Graveyard. The drifting Melina and the Spirit Steed Torrent saw him. Melina was hesitant to choose him but Torrent urged her to. Melina placed healing flasks onto the Tarnished's butt. The amnesiac Tarnished awoke, headed up the stairs and lift and exited the Heroes' Grave, seeing Limgrave, having no memories of his past before arriving at the Lands. He sought not to be Lord, having no purpose, simply a noob. White Mask Varre, a servant of Mohg, mocked the Tarnished, scaring him but informed him to head to Stormveil where Godrick was. Meanwhile Godrick was comparing grafting parts to his subordinates. The Tarnished sees the Tree Sentinel but is knocked onto a stake, the Tree Sentinel shocked that he survived. The lost Tarnished is unable to get anywhere. Melina appears, offering to level him up with his runes in return for taking her to the Erdtree, so she can ascertain her purpose which she has forgotten. The Tarnished realizes that like him, Melina wishes to find her purpose and agrees to help her. As for a name, Melina names him Aseo after the Reedlandish pronunciation of Tarnished, Asebito. Melina hands Aseo Torrent. Aseo attempted to challenge the Tree Sentinel with Torrent but fails. Aseo is unable to make any progress and Patches the Untethered, a bald money motivated merchant (who is free of worldly wants such as greed) and an entity who has a presence in other worlds finds him and takes him under his wing. Aseo sees Patches as a brother and Melina questions why Aseo isn't doing anything to make progress. Patches lets Aseo go on his quest after Aseo refuses to steal from the Nomadic Merchant Kale. However, Patches as a parting gift tricks Aseo into a teleporter chest which takes Aseo into Mistwood Ruins, filled with massive Rune Bears. Patches claiming it's to prepare Aseo for the dangers that lie ahead. Aseo escapes the forest, conversing with Kale, Kale offering Aseo a free crafting kit if he assists Ranni's Shadowbound Beast Blaidd in Mistwood, which Aseo reluctantly does. Blaidd reveals his intentions to kill the Bloodhound Knight Darwil. Aseo and Blaidd befriend and helps Blaidd who has poor directional skills reach Darwil in Forlorn Hound Evergaol where he is imprisoned. Melina translates the fight between Blaidd and Darwil. Both beasts were once allies. Darwil was a Ranni fan and Ranni's adoptive brother Blaidd and him secretly did a Ranni fan club to make Ranni dolls. They even put up a Reedlandish sign for the club. When Darwil decided to give the Ranni dolls maid dresses, this turned them into enemies. Blaidd believes that Darwil being trapped in the Evergaol isn't enough to pay for the crime of what he did to Ranni's dolls. Melina defeats Darwil, sickened at their conversation. Aseo returns to Kale at the Church of Vows, to find Kale sleeping and to see Ranni who claims she is the witch Renna to keep her identity hidden, something Aseo sees through given he had seen Blaidd's Ranni dolls. Ranni gives Aseo a bell to summon spirit summons and also 3 wolf spirit summons which Aseo names Pochi, Shirou and Tarou. Godrick makes plans, wishing to hold a grafting competition. Aseo after some bonding with the wolfs, walks to Stormveil but unlike the previous times the way there is not guarded as Godrick has retracted his troops for the impending competition. Aseo on the way encounters Roderika. Roderika was a noblewoman and a Tarnished, her men were killed by a Grafted Scion, children grafted into monstrous spider like beings by Godrick himself. She has lost any will to survive but Aseo urges her to remain hopeful, sharing his similar experience of being stranded in this strange land. Aseo heads into the outer area before Stormveil where he is met by Morgott as Margit. Aseo tries to summon the wolfs against Margit but they flee. Aseo loses any will to fight and prepares to die. Morgott is shocked, giving Aseo tips on how to properly progress, Aseo calling him Margit the Full Walkthrough. Morgott leaves, asking that Aseo challenge him properly when they meet in the Royal Capital, Leyndell. Aseo encounters Gostoc who seeks to lure Aseo into Godrick's grafting competition, offering Aseo to go by the gate or by the suspicious secret way. Aseo gets a soap which Gostoc is selling. Aseo knocks out Gostoc out of suspicion. Aseo is found by Sorcerer Rogier. Rogier is involved with Fia, the Deathbed Companion, her closest companion. Like Fia, Rogier also seeks to allow those who live in death and to into the Golden Order. Rogier falls into the depths of Stormveil, coming across an extension of Godwyn's Deathroot which impales and infects him. Aseo progresses through the massive castle during which he comes across a Grafted Scion, the same one which killed Roderika's loyal friends. Nepheli Loux, the adoptive daughter of Gideon Ofnir, attempts to kill the Scion. Aseo is thankful but Nepheli suddenly stops, saying that she didn't intend to take Aseo's kill. With the power of soap, Aseo defeats the Grafted Scion. Nepheli and Aseo head through the entrance of the area of the castle and come face to face with Godrick and his forces. Godrick commences the contest. Godrick always wished to be as great as his ancestors, desiring to become an Elden Lord. Believing grafting to grant power, he became obsessed with grafting but at some point did begin to enjoy it. The grafting contest is Nepheli and Aseo on the Tarnished team against Godrick. If they lose they get grafted. For the Tarnished who cannot have the grafting abilities of gods and demigods they get clay. Nepheli likes making clay stuff apparently and wins the grafting competition. Godrick is angered and saddened. His Godrick's followers however, say that Godrick even in his cowardliness they remain loyal. Godrick realizes that in his quest to be as great as his ancestors, he had failed to recognize the loyalty of those around him. Godrick decides to abandon his ambitions, his quest for power, instead deciding to pursue grafting entirely as an art. Godrick abandoning his claims as a demigod, hands Aseo his Great Rune. Rumors begin to spread that the Tarnished Aseo had slain the demigod Godrick. Melina takes Aseo to Roundtable Hold. Where Aseo meets Enia, the Finger Reader, Gideon and Gideon's subordinate Ensha. Gideon initially mistaking Aseo for a noob, thinks lowly of Aseo but is shocked when Aseo shows the Great Rune he obtained. Gideon develops a dislike for Aseo, Aseo telling the hold to hold him a welcome party. Ensha questions if Gideon wishes to kill Aseo, Gideon deciding to save that for Aseo. Aseo also encounters Fia who gives him a Reedlandish back massage, Aseo finding the process painful. Gideon holds the party but Aseo misses. Aseo goes to visit Roderika, who is still at the shack but in a better condition now. Recusant Bernahl shows up wishing to teach Aseo and Roderika some combat skills. Aseo with the skills is told by Melina to head to Caelid. On the way to Caelid, Aseo encounters Alexander, the Warrior Jar. But Aseo is terrified by the rotten creatures there. Aseo is met by Ranni who tries to recruit Aseo into her follower. Aseo refuses. Aseo notices that the Carian Filigreed Crest of the Carian Royal House of Rennala is the Ranni fan club crest, saying its name. Ranni becomes suspicious that Blaidd has indeed started a fan club concerning her. Why? Because Blaidd wasn't supposed to tell everyone that Ranni was alive. Aseo refuses, Ranni tells him to get a Great Rune from her mother Rennala. Aseo enters Liurnia, meeting Thops, a sorcerer who offers him 10 runes for every service. Aseo does learn some magics under Thops such as Thops Barrier. Thops wishes to return to the academy which has closed its doors since the start of the Shattering which was thousands of years ago. Thops needs a Glintstone Key to enter, imploring Aseo's help. Aseo whilst travelling through Liurnia encounters the cowardly Diallos. Diallos is a Tarnished of the noble House Hoslow, the clan head being his older brother Juno. Diallos cries over his servants Lanya's death, with Aseo noting how pathetic and cowardly he is. Diallos believes Lanya was killed by Recusants of Volcano Manor, seeking after it for revenge. Which Diallos is too cowardly to properly execute despite trying to act brave. Aseo on the way to Liurnia encounters Patches once again. Patches defends his previous actions of sending Aseo into Mistwood as preparation and explains that he and his gang are taking crayfish to Godrick for grafting. Aseo also meets the food maker Boggart and Patches' daughter figure Zorayas (Patches is her father figure as her actual father Rykard is a literal snake). Boggart took Zorayas' necklace of her mother Tanith because Zorayas ate his food without payment, Patches solving it by paying. Patches and Boggart also have an argument given the crayfish are Boggart's livelihood. Patches notes that near the Glintstone Dragon Smarag, there's a Glintstone Key which he wishes to sell. Aseo also seeking it agrees with Patches' plan. The plan is to have Aseo distract the dragon and Patches grabs the key. Aseo initially fails to distract the dragon, with Smarag flying at Patches, who admits defeat. Aseo is unscathed by Smarag's attacks, shocking Patches for perhaps the first time. Aseo kills Smarag. Patches hands Aseo the Glintstone Key which Aseo uses to enter the academy where Rennala is. Aseo makes it through the academy, meeting the Red Wolf of Radagon, the wolf after witnessing the dance Aseo and Pochi, Shirou and Taro did, mentions how he had not seen such coordination between pets and masters since the time when Radagon was married to Rennala. Aseo accidentally enters a portal which takes him to the Church of Vows where he sees Miriel Pastor of Vows, a massive turtle who presided over the marriage of Radagon with Rennala that ended the Liurnia Wars. Melina and Miriel provide context on Radagon's relationship with Rennala, citing that why Radagon left Rennala for Marika was never known. The real reason being that Marika had to fuse with Radagon, who had become an entirely separate entity from her before her ascension to godhood. Ranni sends Aseo back to the area near Rennala's room in the academy but not before an argument she has with him of why Aseo ended up at the academy's entrance again. As for Blaidd, Blaidd is tortured by Ranni for setting up a fan club in secret using the Carian Filigreed Crest. Aseo enters the academy and Rennala, now insane initially welcomes Aseo but has Aseo captive with her loyal knight Moongrum, suspecting that Aseo seeks to manipulate Ranni. Rennala holds a battle between Aseo and Moongrum, which Aseo wins using Thops Barrier, earning Moongrum's respect. Moongrum tells Aseo not to kill Rennala as her mind is already long lost and spreads rumors that Aseo has slain Rennala to prevent any from harming her. Aseo finds another Glintstone Key and hands it to Thops. Aseo visits Roundtable Hold again. Gideon is obviously angry at Aseo and gets more annoyed at Aseo, now that Aseo demands yet another party, claiming that Gideon refused to hold it. Aseo actually missed the previous one unknowingly. Blacksmith Hewg is now Roderika's mentor who teaches her spirit tuning, leveling up spirits summons. Aseo and Roderika enter a catacombs, which has Gloveworts needed to level up summons. They defeat an Erdtree Burial Watchdog there and return to Hewg. Gideon actually holds the party but Aseo misses it during the journey to the catacombs with Roderika, further angering Gideon. Aseo receives a Festering Bloody Finger from Varre, who wishes that Aseo to become a Bloody Finger serving Mohg. Aseo is invaded by Bloody Fingers Nerijus, a servant of Mohg and a Sanguine Noble. He also encounters the Bloody Finger Hunter Yura who explains the Mohg's forces as senseless killers consumed by his Cessblood. Yura mistakes Aseo for being a Bloody Finger and attacks Aseo. Both are attacked by Flying Dragon Agheel who Yura defeats. The misunderstanding is cleared up. Aseo encounters the Demi Human Boc, who wishes to be a fashion lord, kicked out of his clan because he altered Chief A's best clothes. Boc's clan is odd for demi humans as there are 2 demi human chiefs, Chief B being the one that holds any real power and it seems B stole A's other clothes, forcing A to wear the clothes rotted by Boc. Aseo defeats Chief B, with Boc getting his mother's sewing kit which a chief had taken prior to his banishment. Boc sees Aseo as a lord, a sentiment Aseo does not return. Boc makes new clothes for Aseo, but Aseo is unable to pay so Melina helps to, causing Aseo to be in debt to Melina. Aseo heads to the Weeping Peninsula where he encounters Irina, the daughter of the leader of Godrick's forces in the area in Castle Morne, Edgar. Irina was sent away due to a conflict involving the Misbegotten slaves in the Castle Morne, with Irina wishing to deliver a letter to her father. Aseo heads to Castle Morne where he delivers the letter to Edgar. Aseo helps Edgar against the massive Leonine Misbegotten, with Edgar being relieved from his duties as a part of Godrick's forces having killed the main Misbegotten behind the threat. Edgar and Aseo find Irina who is dead. Edgar goes insane and thinks that killing Aseo will bring her back, possibly thinking that Aseo killed her. Aseo flees. Shabiri is a mysterious entity associated with the Flame of Frenzy, he wishes to cause a Tarnished to claim the flame and melt all life into one. Shabiri takes Irina's dead spirit and messes with it, making her think she is Hyetta, someone seeking to be a maiden. His intention is to have her draw a Tarnished to take the Flame of Frenzy. Edgar's madness could be linked to Shabiri himself, with Edgar possessing Shabiri Grapes which could cause some kind of connection with the madness inducing Flame of Frenzy. Aseo encounters D, Hunter of the Dead. D is one who seeks to return the Deathroot to the Beast Clergyman Maliketh, seeking to eradicate those who live in death. He was once friends with Rogier but their paths have diverged long since. Rogier and D help Aseo against a Tibia Mariner, a type of those who live in death.

D asks that Aseo meet the Beast Clergyman Gurranq in Dragonbarrow, who is truly Maliketh who wishes to reabsorb the Deathroot which resulted when a stolen portion of the Rune of Death within Godwyn's corpse spread. Aseo hands the Tibias Mariners' Deathroot to Maliketh who grants him an item. Aseo on Torrent heads down Dragonbarrow, into Caelid. Aseo asks the sage Gowry, for information on the Radahn Festival, which Melina forces him to join. Aseo is fearful of Radahn but Aseo requires two Great Runes to enter the capital, where the Erdtree lies. Given Aseo so far only has Godrick's Great Rune, Melina needs Aseo to get Radahn's. Gowry agrees, on condition, Aseo helps him to have Millicent regain her senses. He has Polyanna assist Aseo get the Unalloyed Gold Needle from Commander O'Neil. Aseo on Gowry's request gave Millicent an unfinished Unalloyed Gold Needle, which would allow Millicent to regain her senses and make her way to the Haligtree. Millicent at first tried to attack Aseo, and urged him to leave due to her condition but when Aseo gave her the needle, she eventually accepted it and passed out. When she regained consciousness she explained to Aseo her condition had improved and demonstrated it by jumping high and gave him a Prosthesis Wearer's Heirloom, as thanks before heading on her way. Millicent deeply trusts Aseo for saving her seeing him as a brother. She is beginning to recall her purpose but dimly and she is trying to find out more about her purpose exactly. Aseo sees Blaidd and Alexander who genuinely believe the rumors that Aseo killed Godrick and Rennala. They alongside Melina pressure him into entering the Radahn Festival which Aseo dreads. At the festival Aseo meets Okina, a Reedlandish Samurai Bloody Finger of Mohg, the Tarnished Tragoth, Fia's adoptive father Lionel. Finger Maiden Therolina is also present, a puppet placed by Seluvis. Aseo's brother figure Patches is also there, to kill Tragoth as part of his job from Volcano Manor. Ranni needs Blaidd to kill the now insane Radahn given Radahn is unable to unfreeze the stars, the stars being unfrozen is needed for Ranni to achieve her Age of Stars. Alexander just wants a good fight. At the start all the fighters are unable to attack, running away to regroup. They discuss plans and eventually they managed to deal damage to Radahn. Jerren, Radahn's second in command shows up to help kill the now insane Radahn, believing an honorable death by battle was what Radahn always wanted. Hence fulfilling the purpose of the Radahn Festival which he had organized. With Radahn's powers waning over the years due to the rot build up, it was this festival that truly killed him. Radahn's soldiers chant at his death, believing Radahn attained the death he so wanted. They do not know that Radahn's death completed Miquella's goals for godhood, allowing them to be set in motion. With Miquella's fate to become a god unbound and Miquella obtaining the soul of Radahn, he needs to ascend to divinity. Patches seeing that heading through Radahn's not to kill Tragoth is not worth doing, perhaps because he wasn't paid enough to contend with this, hence evading his job. Aseo obtains Radahn's Great Rune and rumors spread that Aseo slain Godrick, Rennala and Radahn and claimed their Great Runes. Causing Aseo to be famous. With 2 Great Runes Melina tells Aseo to seek the Dectus Medallions. Aseo returns to Roundtable Hold for information. He asks Gideon but Gideon is now so annoyed at Aseo he refuses to tell him anything. Nepheli pressures Gideon to hold a welcome party for her friend Aseo. Aseo encounters Rogier who is with his partner Fia. Rogier and Fia informs Aseo of their intentions to include those who live in death into the Golden Order. Rogier tells Aseo of his fatal Deathroot stab in Stormveil, saying that it is beginning to kill him. Rogier says he will give information on the Dectus Medallions if Aseo joins Ranni. Ranni has access to her Cursemark and Fia needs both Ranni's and Godwyn's Cursemarks to create a Mending Rune which will allow those who live in death into the Golden Order if a Tarnished succeeds Marika as Elden Lord. Missing out the welcome party, Aseo heads to Caria Manor to meet Ranni, meeting Iji along the way. Ranni happily accepts Aseo into her ranks, having been wishing to recruit him but Aseo previously refusing. Aseo is met by Seluvis, Ranni's servant who asks that Aseo give Ranni Amber Draught which will turn Ranni into his personal puppet. He is an Albinauric and Albinaurics cannot have children of their own. Puppets, which are those forcefully transformed by him into spirit summons are as children to him. Aseo is genuinely disturbed. But Seluvis threatens to do so to his friends Nepheli and Roderika so Aseo feels conflicted. Ranni sends Aseo to help Blaidd in Nokron. Blaidd asks Aseo what are his views, on the Golden Order, on becoming Lord. Aseo admits he hasn't really thought of it. Blaidd asking if the Golden Order is truly the way to go. Blaidd tells Aseo if he wishes to be a Lord he must hold his beliefs close to him. Aseo has no interest in becoming a Lord of any kind. Aseo battles a Mimic Tear which Aseo cannot tell apart. It does not help that Melina is willing to take the Mimic Tear as a replacement if the Mimic Tear wins. Aseo defeats it and grabs the Finger Slayer Blade which Aseo was sent to Nokron to get. Ranni needs the Finger Slayer Blade to kill her Two Fingers. Upon returning to Ranni, Aseo informs her about Seluvis' plans. Aseo heads to Seluvis, with a Mimic Tear he picked up from Nokron disguised as Ranni. Aseo claims he had delivered the Amber Draught, turning Ranni into a puppet, offering Seluvis a drink before handing Ranni over. Seluvis realizes that he has been tricked into drinking the Amber Draught. The real Ranni shows up, revealing she and Aseo had planned this. Ranni thanks Aseo for the help with a Sword of Night and Flame. Ranni gives Aseo a key to a tower which allows him to obtain her Cursemark. Aseo after collecting Ranni's Cursemark, returns to Roundtable Hold, where D has been defeated by Fia. Rogier and Fia leave the hold, with Fia revealing her allegiance to Godwyn and asking that Aseo hands her Ranni's Cursemark when they meet again. She needs both Ranni's and Godwyn's Cursemarks to create the Mending Rune of the Death Prince, which will allow those who live in death to exist within the Golden Order.

Gideon who genuinely is irritated enough by Aseo, has Aseo head with Nepheli to find the Haligtree Medallions in the Albinauric Village. Given the lack of communication, Aseo thinks that Gideon was referring to the Dectus Medallions, which Aseo is looking for. Nepheli and Aseo as they head to Liurnia on Torrent, meet a Night Cavalry of Morgott, who sends Aseo Morgott's regards. Aseo and Nepheli find that the village has been ransacked, with all the Albinauric villagers hanged. Nepheli is horrified. It is revealed that Gideon had paid an Omenkiller and a Depraved Perfumer to ransack the village in search of the medallions, seeking that Aseo could get any remaining survivors to speak up. Nepheli is horrified, Aseo defeating the ransackers with the Sword of Night and Flame. Nepheli confronts Gideon about this, Gideon disowning her as useless. Gideon adopted Nepheli as his daughter when she was a lost Tarnished, now without his guidance she is without purpose, shocked and horrified that her father would do such a thing. With no care about the innocent denizens. Nepheli copes by making clay sculptures, which is her hobby, she is stressed nevertheless. Albus, an Albinauric seeing Aseo defeat the ransackers, urges Aseo to take the Haligtree Medallions. It is revealed that the other Albinaurics in the village had been pretending to have died from the torture. The Haligtree Medallions lead to the Consecrated Snowfields, the region leading to the Haligtree, the safe haven the empyrean Miquella created for the oppressed. Albus urges Aseo to give it to Latenna. Unlike her, Albinaurics like him can never make their way to the snowfield. Latenna seeks to deliver Birthing Droplets to her sister Phllia in the Snowfields so her sister can give birth. Aseo returns to the hold and confronts Gideon. Why Gideon did this, why he was willing to subject the village to such horrors. Gideon says that his goal is an unending quest for knowledge, he is willing to do anything for it. Aseo notices the depressed Nepheli, before heading to Latenna in Liurnia. Latenna agrees to Aseo's help, joining Aseo's journey as a spirit summon. Aseo whilst in Liurnia comes across Edgar who seeks to kill him, believing it will bring back his daughter Irina. Hyetta appears, being the spirit of Irina messed with by Shabiri, who seeks that the Flame of Frenzy melt all into one. Edgar and Hyetta have an instant father-daughter connection. But in an eerie twist, Edgar does not seem to recognize Hyetta is his daughter Irina despite acting like she is, something which shocks Aseo, finding it suspicious. Hyetta believing they are needed for her to become a maiden, unaware of the Flame of Frenzy's intentions, accepts Shabiri Grapes from the insane Edgar, also under the influence of the Flame of Chaos. Causing her connection to the Flame of Frenzy to be heightened. Aseo heads up the Bellum Highway, unsure what to do. He has to get into Altus, yet he cannot ascend the Dectus Lift into Altus given he lacks the Dectus Medallions. In this moment, Hyetta offers Aseo an alternative pathway, if he helps her get Fingerprint Grape, a type of Shabiri Grape. Aseo and Hyetta head to the Church of Irith where they encounter Vyke. Vyke hands them the Fingerprint Grape after talking to Aseo about his feats and Aseo's fame as the Greatest Tarnished. Hyetta reveals Aseo the alternative pathway, the Ruin-Strewn Precipice. Aseo heads his way. However Hyetta has Dectus Medallions of her own, encountering Boc. Boc and Hyetta take the medallions up the Dectus Elevator, reaching Altus. Aseo at the Ruin-Strewn Precipice sees Zorayas, Patches and Boggart. Boggart and Patches are arguing. Zorayas informs Aseo that her father figure Patches has been evading his job and he has to bring Patches back to her mother Tanith who is Patches' boss. Aseo, Boggart and Zorayas head up the Ruin-Strewn Precipice and come across Millicent, who sees Aseo as a brother. It is here where Aseo realizes he has made a lot of friends. Millicent informs Aseo that she's still on her way to the Haligtree. She is more aware of her purpose, knowing it is linked to Malenia in some way. She is still trying to figure and remember it. The purpose being Millicent wishes to return herself, being Malenia's will to Malenia, believing that it will restore her individuality. Except she is still recalling and trying to remember this purpose. Aseo, Millicent, Boggart battle their way through the precipice. A Winged Dame grabs Millicent's niece Zorayas however, with a combined attack with Aseo, Zorayas is rescued, Patches barely rescuing her. The group are met with the Magma Wyrm Makar. Magma Wyrms are the results of prolonged Dragon Communion, it is what those that consume dragon hearts for power turn into. Millicent, Aseo, Boggart defeat the Magma Wyrm, but Aseo's clothes are destroyed in her process. The group reaches the Altus. Millicent bids farewell and continued on her journey. Zorayas pressures Patches to the Volcano Manor for his job evasion, whilst Boggart heads to the Capital's Outskirts. Aseo is met by Melina. Now they are in the Altus, their purpose is to reach the capital. Boc shows up discussing how he reached the Altus. Boc is super obsessed with making clothes for Aseo, seeking to be a fashion lord and also having huge gratitude to Aseo for retrieving his sewing kit. Instead of listening to Aseo's suggestions, Boc makes his own fashion design on Aseo which annoys him. Nearby Demi Human Queen Gilika and her clan are watching the Demi Human Boc styling Aseo. Gilika is someone Boc respects. Gilika admires Boc's optimism but calls his fashion sense outdated. Gilika decides to style Aseo herself, with the finished design, she claims representing King Morgott's teachings of love and care. Aseo commenting it instead reflects lunacy. Boc is overwhelmed by the fashion sense of Gilika but says he won't give up and he will be a fashion lord. Aseo annoyed, defeats Gilika. Boc listens to Aseo's suggestions on fashion and armor, giving practical armor and outfit which suits Aseo's needs. Aseo thanks Boc, saying that Boc needs to continue listening to his customers instead of forcing his fashion sense. Boc agrees to learn under the injured Gilika, bidding farewell to Aseo. Gilika only then realizes the fact that Aseo is not a demi human but a Reedlander, because demi humans aren't very intelligent. Or at least they are no longer very intelligent. Melina hands Aseo some weapons and Aseo heads near the Capital Outskirts, where he encounters the monk/prophet Coryhn whom he previously met in Roundtable Hold. Given the gate they are near is heavily fortified, Aseo and Coryhn head elsewhere. Coryhn is looking to learn under the Ever Brilliant Goldmask, the sage seeking to perfect the Golden Order. In Coryhn's view a perfect other is one of comedy. Aseo and Coryhn meet the incredibly stationary Goldmask. Despite being very stationary, Coryhn can interpret Goldmask, Goldmask testing Coryhn and accepting Coryhn as his disciple. Aseo heads to the other gate leading into the Capital Outskirts where he is met by Morgott as Margit. Aseo recalls the challenge Morgott as Margit had set for him previously. Aseo goes all out on Morgott as Morgott wishes, in a climatic battle, which Morgott halts. Aseo seeing Morgott quit also quits. Morgott says that Aseo is much more promising than the many Tarnished he has slain. But Aseo is not strong enough to face off against the Draconic Tree Sentinel which guards the gate of Leyndell. Morgott offers Aseo some areas to farm enemies for strength. One of this includes Dominula Village, which Morgott says is a cheerful and happy, welcoming village, a place to relax when tired. Morgott also informs Aseo, that he won't allow Aseo to enter the capital, unless he defeats Rykard, Lord of Volcano Manor and gets his Great Rune. Now Aseo literally needs to kill Rykard to get into the capital. Melina seeing Aseo is tired, takes him to Dominula. Aseo is genuinely horrified as the villagers of Dominula are insane folks, dancing maniacally. These insane villagers are adherents of the Gloam-Eyed Queen. After her defeat, in ancient times they had served the Golden Order. This village was led by a Godskin Apostle. Melina forces Aseo to dance alongside the insane adherents. Torrent is genuinely horrified. Aseo makes his way to the manor, on the way encountering Alexander who hands him a jar which Aseo puts on. Alexander does it as a gift of thanks, he mentions he was the jar who gave a jar to Jar-Wright who Aseo remembers is a puppet of Seluvis. After receiving the jar, Aseo heads up Gelmir and encounters a Falling Star Beast.

Aseo and his Mimic Tear prepare to take down the Falling Star Beast. This is the first time he summons one and he recalls his fight with a Mimic Tear in Nokron. Aseo notices the tear copied his appearance but seems more elegant. The Mimic Tear is happy to assist, calling him sir and saying all the stuff he got are essentially copied from Aseo. Melina says that she can hardly tell the difference. Aseo notices how the mimic utilizes his skills more effectively than him. He suggests strategies with Aseo and Melina, calling Melina a dame. Melina notes that the mimic has a seemingly stronger bond with Torrent than even Aseo. Melina doesn't mind if the mimic replaces the real deal as long as he gets her to the Erdtree. Melina offers the actual Aseo to act as a mimic to the mimic. Mimic and Aseo defeat the beast, mimic encouraging Aseo and saying that Aseo's level of skill can't be replicated. Aseo sees the Troll guarding the manor and lies and says he wants to kill some Tarnished, the Troll lets him pass.

Aseo ends up in front of Volcano Manor, where he comes face to face with Tanith, wife of Rykard and the de facto leader of the faction. Tanith introduces the manor's goals and Aseo notices a portrait of Rykard. Tanith warns Aseo to watch his mouth otherwise he will be attacked by Ghiza's Wheel. Tanith says Ghiza shaved his whiskers that morning with the wheel, Ghiza saying that his bandages are due to that. Ghiza is constantly involved in surveillance, execution, gruesome rituals…causing his face to fester. They ask for his name, Aseo gives the fake name Osea. They quickly note the name's similarity to the Tarnished Aseo, famed for slaying Radahn, Godrick and Rennala. Zorayas who is here recognizes Aseo, blowing his cover. Ghiza and Crucible Knight attack Aseo who quickly puts on his armor. Tanith does not trust Zorayas around Aseo. Aseo shows Tanith the invitation he received from Liurnia, Zorayas says that Aseo forgot his real name to cover for the fake name. Ghiza notes this is indeed the champion Aseo to Tanith but Tanith agrees feeding Aseo to Rykard would be good. Tanith, Ghiza and the Crucible Knight feign that they genuinely believe Aseo, allowing Aseo to join the manor. Aseo thanks Rya for the help, Rya notes that Patches has gone to find the Dectus Medallion she lost along the way. Aseo now having joined decides to work out a plan, also quickly suspecting he is definitely in a trap. Bernahl sees Aseo and he is shocked at this place kills Tarnished. Aseo initially does not recognize Bernahl due to having his helmet but he soon enough does.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Fingercreepers** are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Aberrant, disembodied hands, Fingercreepers are corrupt children of Metyr, Mother of Fingers, a consequence of an ancient act of blasphemy against the Greater Will. As a result, it is not uncommon to find them near locations of great atrocities, such as Caria Manor, Mt. Gelmir, the lower parts of Leyndell, as well as the Mountaintops of the Giants.

They tend to hide, sometimes high up on walls and sometimes buried underground, ambushing unsuspecting targets. Some fingers bear enormous golden rings with purple gemstones that fire pink projectiles that magically immobilize their prey, then grab and crush them. As they grow, they become immense, nearly indestructible giants. However, their pallid, sinewy flesh is highly flammable—when set ablaze, they roll and thrash violently to extinguish the flames.

- A Stranded Soul at the Finger-Weaver's Hovel determined the Finger Ruins were the source of Fingercreepers.
- Fingercreepers and Two Fingers are siblings.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: This page provides an overview of the **endings** in Elden Ring. Players have six options to conclude the game: the *Age of Fracture*, *Age of Order*, *Age of the Duskborn*, *Blessing of Despair*, *Age of the Stars*, or the *Lord of Frenzied Flame*.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The various endings in Elden Ring are tied to choices made by the player throughout their journey, as well as optional questlines. These outcomes define the fate of the Lands Between, and the role the Tarnished assumes as Queen Marika's Elden Lord or otherwise. Each ending represents the Tarnished brandishing the Elden Ring and ushering in their new Age.
Note**: Receiving the Flame of Frenzy from the Three Fingers in the Frenzied Flame Proscription will **lock** the player out of all endings except the *Lord of Frenzied Flame* ending. This restriction can be lifted by using Miquella's Needle when prompted at Dragonlord Placidusax's boss arena, however, doing so will **permanently lock** the player out of the *Lord of Frenzied Flame* ending.

sections.heading: Choosing an Ending
sections.markdown:
After defeating the final boss, the Tarnished will return to a room containing Marika's statue and a nearby Grace. If Ranni's questline has been completed, her summon sign will also appear near the Fractured Marika statue. At this point, the player can choose an ending by interacting with either Marika's statue or, if available, Ranni's summon sign.

If the Tarnished possesses the Frenzied Flame, Ranni's summon sign will not appear unless the Frenzied Flame has been removed using Miquella's Needle. In this scenario, the only option is to interact with Marika's statue, which automatically triggers the *Lord of Frenzied Flame* ending, offering no alternative choices.

Without the Frenzied Flame, interacting with Marika's statue presents the option to select one of three possible mending runes obtained during the Tarnished's journey. Choosing a rune initiates the corresponding ending: *Age of Order*, *Age of the Duskborn*, or *Blessing of Despair*. Alternatively, players can choose to "Mend the Elden Ring" without a rune, resulting in the *Age of Fracture* ending.

If Ranni's summon sign is present and selected instead of Marika's statue, the *Age of the Stars* ending will begin.

Regardless of the choice, the nearby Site of Grace allows the player to teleport elsewhere and return later, postponing the ending and enabling continued exploration.

To start a New Game Plus, an ending must be selected. After the end credits, players can choose "Begin Journey X" or return later to the Roundtable Hold Grace to initiate the new playthrough.

sections.heading: Elden Lord
sections.markdown: The *Age of Fracture*, *Age of Order*, *Age of the Duskborn*, and *Blessing of Despair* endings all result in the Tarnished becoming Marika's new Elden Lord. Each offers a different interpretation of Marika's vision for the Golden Order, mending the Elden Ring and ushering in their new Age of choice to rule over.

sections.heading: Age of Fracture
sections.markdown: In the *Age of Fracture* ending, the Tarnished becomes Elden Lord without adding any special Mending Runes to the Elden Ring. In doing so, they fulfill the Two Fingers' plans of using the Tarnished to restore the sense of stability not felt since the Elden Ring was shattered. The Golden Order remains in the truest state possible to what it once was and the status quo is restored.

sections.heading: Age of Order
sections.markdown: The Tarnished becomes Elden Lord, fulfilling Goldmask's idea of a "Perfect" Golden Order based on his research into how it had fallen to its current state. Realizing that the Golden Order's imperfections stemmed from the fickleness of the gods, who, in fact, were no better than men, Goldmask's new transcendental ideology attempts to bring true order to the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Age of the Duskborn
sections.markdown: The Tarnished becomes Elden Lord, wielding the rune born from Fia and the Prince of Death's union. Just as the Golden Order had been created by confining the Rune of Death, the Tarnished creates a new order of death restored. The principle of life in death is embedded within this order, and Those Who Live in Death are allowed to live in peace. Thus begins the *Age of the Duskborn*.

sections.heading: Blessing of Despair
sections.markdown: The Tarnished becomes Elden Lord, bringing about an accursed world where defilement becomes the norm. All will become cursed in the *Blessing of Despair* ending. Thus, none can be scorned, fulfilling the Dung Eater's twisted vision.

sections.heading: Age of the Stars
sections.markdown: In the "Age of the Stars" ending, the player Tarnished summons Ranni the Witch to succeed Marika in godhood. Ranni ushers in her vision of a new order not of gold, but of the stars and moon of the chill night. Rather than make herself and her order objects of worship, she chooses instead to keep her order and both the Lands Between and the cycle of life and death at a great divide, removing the certainties of faith that had existed during Marika's rule. The Tarnished takes the role of Ranni's Elden Lord consort, and they leave the Lands Between together, embarking on a thousand-year voyage into darkness under the wisdom of the Moon.

sections.heading: Lord of Frenzied Flame
sections.markdown:
The "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending, triggered by the possession of the Frenzied Flame, overrides the possibility of any other ending. The Tarnished disregard the notion of becoming Elden Lord, becoming the Lord of Frenzied Flame instead and incinerating everything that came before. Rather than become Elden Lord, The Tarnished becomes the Lord of Frenzied Flame, fulfilling the machinations of Shabriri, and the Three Fingers' will. The Tarnished is left almost completely alone, the Frenzied Flame rapidly consuming everything in existence.

If Melina was not sacrificed, she is seen vowing to hunt down and kill the Tarnished for not heeding her earlier warnings. For The Tarnished to separate themselves from the Frenzied Flame's influence after it being inherited, they must acquire Miquella's Needle and follow its specific conditions of use. Once the Frenzied Flame is suppressed, it can not be reclaimed in any way, preventing the *Lord of Frenzied Flame* ending.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The Age of Fracture is the simplest to obtain, only requiring the player to finish the game, while all others demand completion of their respective side quests beforehand.
- The *Lord of Frenzied Flame* ending has an additional bonus ending cutscene if Melina was not sacrificed as a maiden. It shows her finding the burned Spectral Steed Whistle in the ashen ground and stating that she will now follow through with her vow to kill The Tarnished with Destined Death for becoming the Lord of Frenzied Flame.
 - If Melina was sacrificed and The Tarnished became the Lord of Frenzied Flame afterward, the bonus cutscene would simply not play.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- An unused variant of the *Age of Order* ending was titled the *Age Absolute*.
- The *Age of Fracture* has an unused alternate introduction.
- Among the cut content surrounding Miquella the Kind, there was at one point an ending associated with him. Miquella would have offered his dew to the Tarnished and requested their share in his dream. He would have a world where "all things will flourish, whether graceful, or malign." This may imply that this version of Miquella envisioned a world where even marginalized groups, such as Albinaurics and Misbegotten, would thrive.
 - The term "malign" in the English translation does not perfectly align with the Japanese text, which is translated literally as "not-so-graceful."
- The English dialogue for the *Age of the Stars* ending has been debated for its interpretative differences compared to the Japanese script. Some suggest that a more literal translation may provide additional clarity and preserve the nuances of the original text, as discussed here.

sections.markdown: Ensha of the Royal Remains** is an NPC in *Elden Ring*.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Ensha is the unspeaking adherent of Sir Gideon Ofnir, typically found leaning on the wall outside his master's study in Roundtable Hold. Ensha wears armour graced with golden human bones, which are said to have belonged to a soulless king, the lord of the lost and desperate, known as Ensha.

After the Tarnished obtains one half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, Ensha invades them in Roundtable Hold. After killing Ensha, the Tarnished confronts Gideon, who claims that Ensha got ahead of himself. As an apology, Gideon furnishes the Tarnished with advice regarding the whereabouts of the medallion's other half.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Elder Lions**, also known as **Guardian Lions**, are non-respawning Enemies in Elden Ring and Bosses in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Elder Lions are beasts blessed with spiritually-infused horns by the primordial Crucible of life. Valued by the hornsent, lion pelts adorned the bodies of chosen Divine Beast Warriors who invoked divinity to perform tempestuous, cavorting lion dances. Serosh, Lord of Beasts—the hornless golden lion—later became Lord Godfrey's Regent, and symbolized the noble Golden Lineage.

Battered Elder Lions equipped with curved swords once engaged in gladiatorial combat at the colosseums, but the practice died out by the time of Lord Radagon. However, lions were later utilized by various military groups during the Shattering, some supporting lordsworn forces stationed at Leyndell, Redmane Castle, Stormveil, and Castle Sol. Starscourge Radahn, the Red Lion General, and his famed Redmanes practiced the Lion's Claw technique, a battle art that imitated the light-footedness of lions.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
A massive lion with a dark gray coat and fierce yellow eyes, its silvery-white mane decorated by broken horns. Two pairs of manacles are nailed cruelly into its forelimbs, and a curved blade fixed to the right serves as a prosthetic weapon. Bearing the scars of many battles, the chained beast moves with brutal grace, somersaulting forward to cleave its prey with precision.

Elder Lions patrolling Castle Sol can exhale a freezing fog.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.markdown:
Elder Lions are often found in areas associated with the Banished Knights, Starscourge Radahn, and the Golden Lineage.
- Altus Plateau
- Castle Sol
- Fort Gael
- Leyndell, Royal Capital

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The Lion's Claw and Savage Lion's Claw techniques used by General Radahn and the Redmanes visibly emulate the movement of the Elder Lions' somersault strike.
- The Elder Lions have five claws, a celebrated symbol among the Beastmen of Farum Azula, who consider it a sign of the intelligence once bestowed on their kind.
- Golden lions symbolized the Golden Lineage of Elden Lord Godfrey and his Beast Regent, Serosh.
- The Divine Beast is represented by a horned lion.
 - Statues of horned lions line Belurat, Tower Settlement and Enir-Ilim.
 - The sculpted keepers of the tower wore lion pelts to invoke divinity. Enormous lions were used to create the Divine Beast Dancing Lion.
 - The ritual of the lion dance in particular was revered for its divinity, fury, and light-footed beauty.
- Leonine Misbegotten have the appearance of a lion and some imps wear lion masks.

- There are disabled spawn markers for lions at the Colosseums. An elder lion would have battled a Grave Warden Duelist at the Royal Colosseum, a concept likely recycled for the Onestrike Warrior and Blinding Elder Lion encounters in Elden Ring Nightreign.

Evergaols** are a recurring type of location in the Lands Between.

Evergaols appear as a circle in the ground made of gray bricks. Interacting with the symbol at the center will allow you to enter the Evergaol where you will have to fight its inhabitant in a 1-on-1 duel. Once entered, you may not exit an Evergaol without either dying or defeating the boss within.

Ordina, Liturgical Town is an exception, as it uses the Evergaol mechanic for the area's puzzle, rather than the Evergaol containing a boss.

With the exception of summoning Blaidd the Half-Wolf inside of the Forlorn Hound Evergaol, it's impossible to summon anyone, cooperator or Spirit Ash, inside of an Evergaol.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Eternal Cities** are landmarks in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The Eternal Cities of the Lands Between are buried deep underground. The city of Nokstella rests along the Ainsel River Main, while Nokron is perched on a plateau overlooking the Siofra River. These cities are inhabited by the Nox and their Silver Tears, or patrolled by scouting Fallen Hawks. An uninhabited, third nameless Eternal City lies in ruins below the Prince of Death's Throne in the Deeproot Depths.

sections.heading: List of Eternal Cities
sections.markdown:
- Noklateo, the Shrouded City
- Nokron, Eternal City
 - Siofra Aqueduct
- Nokstella, Eternal City
- The Nameless Eternal City

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
]]

The Eternal Cities were built by the Nox, who were devoted to the starry night sky. These cities contained massive stone Chair-Crypts that seated giant maidens. The Nox used weapons forged from the liquid metal of Silver Tears, which could mimic other forms. They used these Mimic Tears in an attempt to create their own Lord.

Long ago, the Nox conspired against the Greater Will. They donned Nox Mirrorhelms to repel its light and used the Fingerslayer Blade to inflict a grievous wound upon a vassal of the Greater Will. As punishment for their blasphemy, they were banished deep underground. The Black Moon that hung over Nokstella was shattered into Memory Stones, and Astel, Naturalborn of the Void was unleashed upon one of their cities and it stole its false night sky. Although the nameless Eternal City was completely leveled, the others were left mostly intact. Although the efforts of the Nox all ended in failure, they continued to believe a Lord of Night would one day come to usher in an Age of the Stars.

Eternal City architecture also appears in Sellia, Town of Sorcery, Ordina, Liturgical Town, Leyndell, Royal Capital, and the Ainsel River Main.

sections.heading: Inhabitants
sections.markdown:
- The Eternal Cities were home to the Nox clergy, which included Nox Monks, Nox Swordstresses, and Night Maidens.
- Silver Tears are found throughout Nokron and Nokstella.
- The Fallen Hawks now wander Nokron and the Siofra Aqueduct.
- The Dragonkin Soldiers, who wielded ice lightning, were born in the Eternal Cities after they were sent underground.
- The Nox of the nameless Eternal City crafted Valiant Gargoyles with Corpse Wax.
- War Counselor Iji wears a Mirrorhelm, the description of which either implicates his involvement in the plot to use the Fingerslayer Blade or his knowledge of it and his blasphemous desire to use it for Ranni's plans.
- The nameless Eternal City is populated by Basilisks, Mausoleum Knights and Mausoleum Soldiers and Gargoyles.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Many of the buildings constructed by the Nox, such as the Siofra Aqueduct, appear inverted, hanging like stalactites from the cavern ceiling. It is unclear whether these were built after their banishment.
 - The Carian Study Hall was built with a similar design.
- Eternal City ruins are strewn about the Ainsel River Main near Nokstella. This area is red with scarlet rot and prowled by a Baleful Shadow during Ranni the Witch's questline. An aqueduct drains water from the Ainsel into the stagnant lake.
- Sellia, Town of Sorcery was founded in Caelid. Many notable glintstone sorcerers came from Sellia, including Primeval Sorcerer Lusat, who went on to found the Olivinus conspectus at the Academy of Raya Lucaria. The Sellians were known assassins who utilized night sorceries to hunt their peers. The secret chair-crypt at this location is vacant.
- The Eternal Cities were likely buried after the ancient dynasty ended, as they are found surrounded by their underground ruins.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - The nameless Eternal City is the only one without a chair-crypt.

Endurance** is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Endurance stat directly affects their Stamina totals. Leveling Endurance will also increase the Tarnished's Robustness, which increases their resistance to Hemorrhage and Frostbite. Finally, Endurance also affects the Tarnished's possible Equip Load, increasing it as Endurance increases.

The Tarnished can level Endurance by spending Runes at Sites of Grace. Endurance has three soft cap points for increasing Stamina, at 15, 30 and 50, with increases seeing dimishing returns after these points. Increasing Robustness sees two soft caps, 40 and 60, with gains from increasing Endurance not beginning until 31 Endurance. Increasing Equip Load sees soft caps at 25 and 60 Endurance.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Equip Load** is one of the stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Equip Load affects their movement speed, and increases as the Tarnished equips more items in their equipment slots. It will also affect the amount of invincibility frames and recovery frames, with heavier equipped loads affecting them negatively. More specifically, Light Load rolls and Medium Load rolls are equally effective and have the same recovery time, but the former will roll a longer distance. Heavy Load rolls meanwhile face an almost twice as long recovery animation, leaving the Tarnished very vulnerable to follow-up attacks.

Equipped items totalling less than 30% of the maximum equip load is considered a Light Load. Greater than 30% and less than 70% is considered a Medium Load. Greater than 70% is considered a Heavy Load. The game menu will display the Tarnished's current load type directly under the numerical weight totals.

Exceeding 100% weight load will result in being Overloaded, rendering the Tarnished unable to roll or backstep, instead only staggering forward slightly with no benefit.

Equip Load exceeding 70% also increases the time it takes to recover Stamina as well and increases harm caused by fall damage.

The Tarnished can increase their maximum Equip Load by leveling Endurance. Equip Load experiences soft caps at 25 and 60 Endurance, resulting in diminishing returns as leveling increases past these points.

A Prophet has the lowest starting equip load due to its starting Endurance of 8, while the Samurai has the highest due to its Endurance being at 13.

While all other classes start in Medium Load thanks to their starting equipment, the Vagabond is the only class to start in Heavy Load due to its heavy equipment.

The scaling is strongest early on, around 1.5-1.6 per point of Endurance below 26 points in the Attribute before falling off from 26 to 38 Endurance before recovering and averaging 1.5 from 39 to 60 Endurance before falling down 1.0 Equip Load per point of Endurance above 61.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Finger Maiden Therolina** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Therolina is a Finger Maiden who never met the Tarnished she was meant to guide, even though it was promised that the guidance of grace would ensure that the pair be brought together. At some point, she met her end at the hands of Preceptor Seluvis, being turned into one of his puppets. Her puppet will attend Radahn's Festival, presumably under the control of Selivus, to give a lending hand in felling the demigod. Before battling the demigod, Therolina's puppet can be spoken to, but only responds in a silent polite bow.

Upon delivering Seluvis's Potion to any of the potential targets for Selivus, and then discovering his secret chambers, the Tarnished can chose to receive Therolina's puppet as a gift, or purchase it for 2 Starlight Shards. She uses healing incantations and Holy Water Pots, but she is not a fighter by nature and is ill-suited to battle.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - Despite Therolina's puppet already attending the Radahn Festival, the protagonist can also summon their own separate version of Therolina's puppet if they received it from Selivus beforehand.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Fallingstar Beast** is a reoccurring boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Fallingstar Beasts are creatures formed of shiny black rock. They have spiky tails, patches of white fur, and insect-like mandibles. They are found in craters, likely indicating that they plummeted onto the Lands Between from a great distance.

The more mature Full-Grown Fallingstar Beast have greater magical abilities, able to control gravity in their vicinity and unleash great magical beams akin to Comet Azur.

They can use Gravity-based abilities, much like other enemies associated with meteors and fallen stars such as Alabaster Lords, Onyx Lords, and Withered Astel. Much like those other enemies, they are also weak to gravity-based sorceries. Additionally, extraterrestrial weapons such as the Wing of Astel and the Alabaster Lord's Sword and gravity imbued weapons such as the Starscourge Greatsword and Radahn's Spear greatarrows deal bonus damage to these foes.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Fire Monk** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Warrior-monks who reside in the Mountaintops of the Giants. During the War Against the Giants, the Fire Monks fought on behalf of the Erdtree. They devised "Flame, Protect Me", an incantation which shielded the champions of the Erdtree from the Giants' Flame. After the war had concluded, the flame of ruin was sealed away, and the Fire Monks were appointed to watch over it. They were led in this ordeal by the Fire Prelates, and in turn led the Guilty; exiled criminals who wielded thorn sorceries.

After many years, the Fire Monks succumbed to the allure of the flame of ruin, beguiled by it. Wielding fire-based incantations, the Fire Monks continued to keep watch over the flame, bearing the likeness of the fell god upon their chestplates.

At some point, the incantation "Flame of the Fell God", which had been kept secret by Chief Guardian Arghanthy, was stolen by a thief named Adan. Several Fire Monks travelled to Liurnia of the Lakes to seek him out, erecting camps in the lands on either side of the lake while they searched.

A Flame Monk named Amon fled his duty to watch over the Giants' Flame out of cowardice, instead swearing fealty to the god-slaying black flame. He was followed by others, enthralled by the black flame, who became known as Blackflame Monks.

sections.markdown: Fallen Hawk Soldiers** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Fallen Hawks are company of slaves from Stormveil once ordered to explore the Eternal City. When the last of their embers had been used up, they resorted to burning the bones of their fellows for light. This led to them acquiring Ghostflame, but sealed their fates as dwellers of the underground rivers for eternity. An upside-down, perpetually falling hawk serves as their emblem.

The soldiers are pale and skeletal in appearance, lacking armour aside from a few who wear crude helmets. They are missing eyes, and their noses have worn away. They appear to have holes drilled into their heads. The soldiers wield a variety of armaments, including spears, swords, greatshields, heater shields, ghostflame torches, and bows that fire arrows tipped with ghostflame. Their methods are somewhat crude, yet they work well together as a squadron.

- The Archer Ashes found in Nokstella imply that some Fallen Hawks also reached the other Eternal City.
- Due to the demoralizing name and imagery of their emblem, the Fallen Hawks were once the original members of Stormveil before the Storm Lord's defeat at the hands of Godfrey and the Golden Order's seizure of their castle.

Eochaid was a lesser foreign kingdom located outside the Lands Between. Its people were proud ascetics who practiced a distinct form of magic and lived solitary lives. By using copper as a conduit, those from Eochaid willed their blades to pirouette through the skies. The state of Eochaid and its people vanished long ago.

After the Shattering war subsided, a man in iron armor from Eochaid began amassing Bell Bearings, stalking numerous merchants and instructors and killing them with violent corkscrew attacks. When captured, the Bell Bearing Hunter’s crimes warranted the death sentence, and he was bound in winding, rusted iron thorns. Before his execution at The Shaded Castle, Elemer of the Briar seized the ceremonial copper Marais Executioner's Sword, furnishing it with battle skills from his homeland, and drove Castellan Maleigh Marais from the castle, claiming both for himself.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **fell god**, also known as the **one-eyed god**, is a character mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The nameless god of fire is the source of the Giants' Flame and Giants' Flame incantations. While this character is never officially labeled an outer god, it operates in much the same manner as one; however, it interferes with the Lands Between more directly. It is an ancient, malformed deity that was said to possess curled horns and thick braids of bright red hair. It has a single eye with a fiery-orange iris that swirled like an inferno. Surrounding its central pupil is a ring of eight smaller pupils.

It physically manifests as a grotesque visage on the torso of Fire Giants, channeling its immense power through them. Its great flames erupt from a gaping mouth on the host's stomach, unleashing destructive fire upon its enemies.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The fell god of fire has been around for a long time and predates the Erdtree. It was a malevolent figure in the old hornsent legends of Enir-Ilim. The Fire Giants were its followers, and tended the god's undying flames housed within the great black Forge anchored to the Flame Peak atop the Mountaintops of the Giants. Though it was feared, the sparks of its flame could fertilize even frozen lands, leading to the growth of half-ashen and smoldering flowers called Fire Blossoms.

The Fire Giants considered smithing a divine ritual, and even the Trolls, their descendants, wielded hammers as ceremonial tools for smithing, crafted with the same pattern of the fell god's eye. The connection of smithing to divinity dates back to the Forges of the Ancient Ruins of Rauh, where Anvil Hammers were shaped like altars and used in ancient divine rituals.

The fell god was also considered evil by Queen Marika, as its Flames were capable of burning her Erdtree. Thus, she waged a bloody War Against the Giants for the sake of her new Age of the Erdtree. However, during this conflict her priests would be forced to use the very power they were fighting against to protect the champions of the Erdtree from the flames of the Fire Giants, creating the first incantation of the Fire Monks.

It is said that Queen Marika personally slew the fell god, but once the Fire Giants were defeated, she realized the flame of their forge could not die and thus sealed it away, reducing its once formidable fire into mere embers and cursing the last surviving Fire Giant to keep them so for all eternity. The power to fully burn the Erdtree was lost when the Rune of Death was sealed in Maliketh's Black Blade.

However, the fell god was not destroyed. Though dormant, it continued to lurk within its subjects, on the cusp of being awakened at any moment with a sufficient sacrificial offering. The fell god's allure swayed even the Fire Monks that were tasked with keeping watch over the Flame.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:

- It is unclear whether the fell god is one of the outer gods. Though the power of their flames can certainly be described as divine and they operates like one, it is never explicitly stated to be an outer god.
 - Erdtree prophets glimpsed its flame within their faith, implying this power currently exists within the Golden Order.
 - This can be explain by the fact that the forces of the Erdtree were forced to create incantations that channeled the flame of the fell god through faith to protect themselves from that power, thus integrating the laws of another god into the Order. This is something that, according to Sorcerer Rogier, the Golden Order of the past was already capable of doing.
 - In addition, the Erdtree was once as warm as the gentle sun, a power possibly related to those of the fell god
- It currently manifests as a grotesque face on the torsos of Fire Giants.
- In addition to the Fire Giants, the Fell God dwells within the Flame of the Fell God. This spell is a massive ball of fire, not unlike a sun. This ability is most similar to the Messmer's Orb.
- The inhabitants of the Lands Between have produced a number of objects that invoke the fell god's image.
 - The Furnace Golems are colossal wickermen filled with burning bodies. Their faces are Furnace Visages—stone masks depicting the fell god as a bronze sun, with a mane of eight curled horns. It looms high above the Fire Giant faces attached to the golems' knees.
 - Its opens one or both eyes when taking damage or during certain attacks.
 - The sun medallion on the Dung Eater's Omen Armor resembles the Furnace Visage.
 - The leader of the Fire Monks, Chief Guardian Arghanthy, uses a One-Eyed Shield that expels flame from its mouth. The large swirl along below the barrel is flanked by eight smaller swirls.
 - The Fire Monk Armor portrays a cyclopian face on the torso in imitation of Fire Giants.
- The fell god is represented by a ring of eight small circles surrounding a larger central circle.
 - This pattern appears on the One-Eyed Shield, Furnace Visage, Verdigris Armor, and Verdigris Greaves.
 - This distinctive pattern appears on the Divine Towers, with some pillar reliefs featuring central cavities filled with glowing meteorite ore.
 - The Troll's Hammer, used by giants during an age when smithing held divine significance, also features eight circles orbiting a central circle.
 - The Verdigris Discus shares this pattern with the fell god's eye. Verdigris, believed to be a gift from an outer god, also appears on the talismans and great dish carried by the Fire Giant.
 - St. Trina's prophesied adult form shared many physical traits with the fell god.
- The fell god's red hair grows on its followers, such as the Fire Giants, Monks, and Prelates.
 - Radagon, Messmer, Rykard, Radahn, Ranni, Malenia, Millicent, and Millicent's Sisters all have the same red hair. Melina's hair is much more faded than the rest.
 - Red hair also appear on every single Fire Knight, those who had received inside them the flame of Messmer, who had visions of the Flame burning the Erdtree and the kindling inside him.
 - Radagon resented his own red hair, which was a curse of the giants.
 - Misbegotten, especially Misbegotten Warriors, have red hair and fur.
 - Red is a color strongly associated with life and the Crucible, and is the color of the horned Great Red Bears.
 - Red hair appears to seep from the severed Omen horns protruding from the Dung Eater's armor. The only opening in the Omen Helm is a large crack near the right eye.
 - Although inaccessible through normal gameplay, the Dung Eater has faded red hair and is only character modeled to have a deformed facial appearance.
 - The blind Lamenter has horns, red hair, and a dormant face resting on its back. Though its blissful state was a true form of enlightment, the fearful horsent refused to accept it and foolishly buried it deep underground in the Lamenter's Gaol.
- It is commonly referred to as being "grotesque," "corrupt," "malformed," "fell," and "evil."
 - Milos the giant was also seen as malformed.
- Fire Sprites are naturally the most boisterous of their kind.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- In the Japanese localization for Burn, O Flame!, the Fire Giant is singular rather than plural, implying the fell god did not curse them prior to the War Against the Giants, rather it was the curse that Queen Marika the Eternal imposed on the last of their kind, as confirmed in the Remembrance of the Fire Giant's description.
- While the English localization claims that the Hornsent's sagas were "haunted" by the Fell God, the Japanese description simply claims it was "An evil god of fire of the legends of the horned people" (角人たちの伝承にある、火の悪神である). The god of fire being considered as "fell" (evil) could be attributed to Messmer's soldiers who built the Furnace Golem, as the people of Erdtree viewed all deities other than Marika negatively and had a tradition of addressing the deity as "fell" through multiple artifacts.
