sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Generally leans towards Dexterity-scaling over Strength-scaling.
- Despite the description this dagger actually has higher Faith-scaling and raw Attack Power (AP) on a Sacred affinity than on a Flame Art affinity. It's also outclassed in raw AP by a Flame Art affinity Erdsteel Dagger.
 - However, the Fire Knight's Shortsword's Flame Art affinity usually has higher effective damage than the Sacred affinity due to only having to bypass 2 flat defences rather than 3, and the Fire damage will be higher on its own than either the Sacred affinity's Holy damage or the Flame Art Erdsteel Dagger's Fire damage.
- Surprisingly enough, since this weapon is themed after Faith and Fire, it actually has the strongest Intelligence-scaling of all Daggers on the Magic and Cold affinities.
- Though the innate Fire damage is low on all but the Fire and Flame Art affinities, simply having it means it will immediate reset fully applied Frostbite on the next hit if on a Cold affinity or using Frostbite-causing skills such as Chilling Mist. It will also stun enemies that are extremely vulnerable to fire, such as Fingercreepers and Miranda Sprouts and Blossoms
- Has a unique double-hitting heavy attack shared with the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger.
 - This unique attack grants 4 points towards the scaling of the Winged Sword Insignias instead of the usual 2, due to hitting twice.
- If choosing any of the Magic, Cold, Blood, Poison, or Occult affinities this is one of the few weapons that can scale with four separate stats.
 - In the base game the ability to scale with four different stats via affinities was only held by the Clayman's Harpoon and the Erdsteel Dagger, while the DLC added the Black Steel Greathammer, Bloodfiend's Arm, and Fire Knight's Greatsword, weapons which all have the same quality.

sections.markdown: Electrocharge** is an incantation spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Loot:** Fog Rift Catacombs
- Found by dropping down a hole in the second cubicle on the left at the third dropping spike-roof and then taking a left twice to find it in the same rooms as a Catacombs Sorcerer, some Fulgurbloom, and a few Skeletal Slimes.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Summons a lightning bolt down onto the user, damaging nearby enemies with Lightning Attack Power equal to 213% of Incantation Scaling.

For 45 seconds, the user is granted a Body Buff that has Lightning Attack Power equal to 45% of Incantation Scaling in a small area around the user every 1 second.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power of the initial bolt to 262% of Incantation Scaling and the Attack Power of the Body Buff's pulses to 59% of the same.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 28 points of Stamina to cast. Cost is increased to 36 points of Stamina if charged.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
 - Since charging the spell increases the Attack Power of the bolt by 23% and the Attack Power of the lingering effect by 31%, this leads to a total Attack Power increase of 41% and 51% respectively.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- The initial bolt deals surprisingly good damage, if only in a very small area around the user, while the buff deals minuscule amounts of damage.
 - While the damage over time is very small, it is still somewhat useful for things that only require any amount of damage without having to "waste" a hit, such as killing Skeletons before they can resurrect or breaking the damage-reducing bubble from Opaline Bubbletear or a Uplifting Aromatic (including the one used by Perfumers).
 - Annoyingly enough, this lingering damage effect will not prevent the Stance of any enemy from recovering.
 - The lingering damage effect from the Buff completely ignores Guarding, fully piercing through Guarded Damage Negation.
- Since this incantation grants a Body Buff, it will remove many strong defensive buffs such as Barrier of Gold and Fireproof Dried Liver. While there isn't a lot of overlap between these spells' uses (Electrocharge is more suited for use against many smaller enemies, while most defensive buffs are better against tougher foes), this is still a downside to trying to use the initial bolt offensively.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Fire Knights were an order of warriors who answered directly to Messmer the Impaler. Each knight descended from noble families of the Erdtree's high society but was exiled from their homes after pledging loyalty to Messmer. They alone understood their master's cursed serpent-like flames and the Base Serpent that consumed him.

Although they made use of their fire to commit atrocities and destruction in the crusade into the Realm of Shadow, they successfully convinced their lord to preserve the Ancient Ruins of Rauh and its artifacts. The Fire Knight would guard and manage the Storehouse inside the Shadow Keep where ancient specimens and relics were conserved and studied.

After the Elden Ring was shattered and its effects were felt in the Shadow Realm too, the Fire Knights would discover and use the Wrath from Afar incantation that replicated the golden shockwave feared as a sign of the Erdtree's wrath but still used the ancient sigil of the primordial Erdtree.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
The Fire Knights are tall and lanky, with red hair like Messmer, and a trace of soot covering their otherwise unblemished faces.

They wear bright crimson pointed hoods and cloaks, with dark red underarmor. Their chestpieces are engraved with fingerprint-like whorls, while their black scale skirts are lined with gold. They wear braided cord aprons and cuts of rope, both depicting spirals. Their capes bear the emblem of Messmer's Army in gold, over which hangs a large coiled snake and three sets of triplet bells, fastened to the twin golden serpents forming a ring around their necks—symbolic of their bond to Messmer.

In battle, Fire Knights specialize in wielding fire for their master's cause. They fight with greatswords and shortswords, whose slender, spiraling blades undulate like flame. When not striking with steel, they rely on Messmer's Flame and Erdtree incantations, often channeling them through the sacred seal, which strengthens their pyromancies.

sections.markdown: Fire Knight Wego**, or **elder Wego**, is an enemy character in Shadow of the Erdtree. He is a Fire Knight found in the Church District at the Shadow Keep and attacks using Messmer's Flame incantations. He does not respawn after being defeated.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Wego was a venerable leader among the Fire Knights who served directly under Messmer the Impaler. This order was known for their crimson cloaks and golden twin serpents coiled around their necks, symbols of their bond to their master. Like his juniors, old Wego understood Messmer's cursed, serpent-like flames and the torment that consumed him. Wego was once a member of one of the esteemed noble families of the Erdtree's high society but was exiled after pledging his loyalty to Messmer.

Wego’s helmet was unique, adorned with two death masks layered one upon the other. Following the Crusade, Wego turned to the spirituality of Messmer's flames to escape his growing loneliness. He performed rites to resurrect the dead, but the soulless beings he revived offered no comfort to his poor heart.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: Fire Knight Wego is found within a cathedral in the Church District of the Shadow Keep. This area is only accessible after the water has been drained.

sections.heading: Notes

- Wego performs a ritual to revive several Burning Putrid Corpses, which explode in Messmerfire when they approach the player.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Greyoll is revered as the mother of many lesser dragons. She appears as a colossal, immobile dragon in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow, just south of Fort Faroth.

Her body is bent with age, her scales are grey, and silver hairs grow from her jaw like a wizened beard. Though incapable of movement, she lets loose fearsome roars that damage nearby foes. Greyoll depends on her brood for protection and will perish if they are slain.

sections.heading: Locations

- Defeating Elder Dragon Greyoll unlocks Greyoll's Roar, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for three Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- While the English localization claims that Greyoll was the mother of "all" dragons, the Japanese description simply claims she was a "great mother of dragons" (竜の大母).

- Elder Dragon Greyoll was originally intended to be fought more directly. However, attempting to view this moveset results in heavy lag and slowdown which is presumably why it wasn't implemented.
- Greyoll was initially conceived as an Ancient Dragon, with her concept art depicting her as such and the Chinese CNT version of Greyoll's Roar describing her as an "ancient dragon" and a stony mountain. It's likely that this late-stage script revision is the reason she uses a scaled up drake model rather than having a unique design.

sections.heading: Plot

Nightreign* takes place in the Lands Between on a timeline parallel to the events of *Elden Ring*, branching from the Shattering. The Night's Tide, an encroaching wall of violet flames and relentless rain, threatens the land of Limveld and its Roundtable Hold. A Priestess in a hooded white robe and silver mask urges the Nightfarers to unite and prevent an impending catastrophe. Players must survive two nights before facing the Nightlord beyond a door on a petrified tree.

sections.heading: Gameplay
sections.markdown:
Elden Ring Nightreign* delivers a fast-paced roguelike experience, playable solo, duo, or in groups of three.
 Players select one of eight unique classes and must survive two perilous nights in a procedurally generated world before confronting the Night Lord. The game combines cooperative survival with a shrinking safe zone, blending elements of *Elden Ring's* iconic design with new features to enhance replayability. The compact game world draws inspiration from *Elden Ring's* Limgrave and features randomized elements, such as structure layouts, enemy placements, and environmental modifiers. Special map events, including meteoric impacts, ant swarms, and volcanic eruptions, create dynamic scenarios. Sites of Grace and Runes return, allowing players to level up and gain abilities as they progress or fail. Additional mechanics, such as powerful ultimate abilities and new traversal options, expand gameplay possibilities. Players can summon a spectral bird to glide through the sky or scale walls by jumping.

Each of the three nights lasts approximately 10 to 15 minutes. Players begin each run at level 1, simplifying progression and encouraging quick engagement without build optimization. The Night's Tide shrinks the safe zone each night and recedes at dawn. Players caught in the rain take damage, and while daytime deaths allow respawning, nighttime deaths do not.

sections.heading: Key features
sections.markdown:
- **Offline solo or online co-op** - Join forces with up to two other players or venture solo with scaled difficulty.

- **Playable heroes** - Select from one of eight different characters, each with their own story, strengths, and weaknesses. Team composition and coordination will play a key role in determining success.

- **Fast-paced roguelike** - Inputs for movement and combat are more fluid and agile. Players run faster and may wall-jump, vault ledges, and glide around the game world.

- **Dynamic, compact world** - The game world is smaller and will reshuffle with each new run, randomizing locations and encounters.

- **Survive the night** - Each night culminates in a shrinking safe zone and a challenging, randomized boss fight, offering rare loot and selectable rewards.

- **Simplified inventory** - The inventory screens will be color-coded and streamlined, and most items will not persist between runs.

- **Near-Death** - Players are downed and can be revived after their HP drops to 0.

Nightreign* will offer ten playable Nightfarers with unique abilities and impactful ultimates, each named for their character class. These classes are beginner-friendly and more easily defined, but their facial appearance may not be adjusted with the character slider. However, the armor of these characters may be customized with various cosmetics. Each hero has a custom storyline; characters that were not selected can be interacted with at the Roundtable Hold.

sections.heading: Bosses and enemies

The game will feature eight new bosses. Among the new additions is Gladius, a monstrous hound with three heads. Several enemies and bosses return from the original game, such as the Zamor Knights, Godrick Knights, and Demi-Human Swordsmen. Margit, the Fell Omen pursues players across the map and grants a powerful Favor of the Night buff if defeated. In addition, the Centipede Demon, The Duke's Dear Freja, and Nameless King return from *Dark Souls,* *Dark Souls II,* and *Dark Souls III*, respectively. All encounters are randomized, and defeated enemies are not reset upon resting at a Site of Grace. The Night Lord is selected at the Roundtable Hold before the start of each run.

sections.heading: Inventory changes
sections.markdown:
Items and gear are color-coded based on rarity. New items and weapons are available, including lootable skills, upgrades, and stat buffs. Rather than using a generic ball of light, these items are rendered as generic, glowing objects that indicate their item type.

The inventory screens are simplified, and up to three weapons can be equipped in each hand. Randomized passive bonuses from special weapons persist when the item is in the inventory. Weapon weight penalties and stat requirements are removed, but some items have level requirements. Basic loot is shared between players, but special item drops are not.

Items may be purchased from Nomadic Merchant spirits scattered around Limveld. They sit beside a campfire and a smithing anvil. Armaments may be improved with Smithing Stones at these workbenches.

Most items do not persist between runs. Murk can be used to purchase unlockable items that persist between runs, such as cosmetics, emotes, and build-defining Relics. Relics are also obtained at the end of each run, regardless of victory.

sections.heading: Multiplayer
sections.markdown: Nightreign* is primarily designed for 3-player co-op, but offers single-player and two-player modes with reduced enemy scaling. The password system will return to handle private matchmaking. Multiplayer activities are no longer limited by in-game items or confined to a single area or dungeon. Players may communicate through a more robust gesture and ping system. Downed players are revived after taking enough damage from their teammates, but the game ends when all players are downed simultaneously. Unsuccessful runs will spawn Red Phantoms in the worlds of others that may be defeated for valuable loot. Basic loot is shared with teammates, but special boss loot is not. The game will not include player-versus-player (PvP) elements.

sections.heading: Development
sections.markdown: Nightreign* is directed by Junya Ishizaki, a veteran of FromSoftware since *Dark Souls*. The game retains the franchise's hallmark epic battles while introducing a faster-paced combat system. The project was green-lit by Hidetaka Miyazaki, who gave creative control to Ishizaki. , who was heavily involved in the development of *Elden Ring*, did not provide additional contributions for *Nightreign*. The game was conceptualized while *Elden Ring* was still in development.

sections.heading: Part 1:
sections.markdown:
After accepting the remembrance quest from your journal, you'll need to **talk to the Raider** in the Roundtable hold, who will inform you that you should **speak to Wylder**.

Wylder can be found in the room past the Journal room. **Head back to the Raider** afterwards.

Go on any expedition and an objective will appear on the **southwestern** part of the map opposite of where you spawn.

Approach the area and prepare to fight a few opponents. We recommend killing a few enemies on the way to raise your level to make the fight more manageable. Three Guardians of the Dew will spawn and prevent you from obtaining the Golden Dew. After that you will get Golden Dew.
Speak to Wylder** and show him the Golden Dew, who will thank you.
Return to the Raider** afterwards and he will task you to **speak to the Revenant** on the western side of the Roundtable.

Head on over to the Revenant and **speak with her**, who will then **direct you towards the Iron Menial** in the Visual Codex room. A ghostly spring will appear next to the Iron Menial after speaking with him. Interact with it to **conclude the remembrance** and you'll receive the **Golden Dew** as a reward.

sections.heading: Part 2:
sections.markdown:
After the remembrance quest starts, you will need to **look for Wylder**. He can be found slumped against the left wall by the Roundtable Hold. **Proceed to the dining room, exit through the hole and take a right** to find Wylder.

Choose to **eat from Wylder's Pita Bread**, and he will speak to you afterwards.
Locate the Iron Menial,** he will be next to the dresser and talk to him regarding Wylder's Pita Bread.

After completing this objective, a ghostly spring will appear for you to conclude this remembrance episode. This will grant you **Duchess' Chalice** as a reward.

sections.heading: Part 3:
sections.markdown:
The Raider will be located in the dining room. **Speak with him** and he will inform you of Weathervane after telling him that you shouldn't fight the Nightlord. After that you need to go on the southeastern beach and speak with Revenant. You must now **defeat Revenant in a duel**. This fight is similar to Revenant's unlock quest, and can be treated the same way. You can also repeat this fight as many times as needed if you die.

After go on any expedition with your Remembrance active and an objective will appear on the **northeastern** part of the map. Approach the area and three Fallen Mercenaries will spawn and prevent you from obtaining Weathervane's Words. Claim the item after defeating them.
Speak to Raider** and show him Weathervane's Words, who will then give you the agency to choose your own path. A ghostly spring will appear next to the Raider. Interact with it to **conclude the remembrance** and you'll receive the **Crown Medal** as a reward.

sections.heading: Part 4:
sections.markdown:
When the Remembrance starts, it is time to bless the Iron Coin at the table of lost grace. Walk up and **interact with the table**.

Head on over to the Iron Menial and **give him the Blessed Iron Coin**. You can find him in the catacombs and can be accessed by going down the stairs from the Visual Codex room, then taking a u-turn left to another set of stairs.
Speak to the Wylder** afterwards. He can be located by the fireplace near the outfit wardrobe.
Return to the Iron Menial** to complete the Remembrance. A ghostly spring should appear next to the Iron Menial to conclude it after.

You will receive both **Duchess' Remembrance Outfit** and the **Blessed Iron Coin** as a reward.

sections.markdown: The **Eclipse** is a recurring event mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The sun in eclipse was a dreadful, mesmerizing sight. Drained of its color, it was a bulwark against Destined Death and held the power to imbue life into soulless bones. The symbol of Castle Sol and the Wandering Mausoleums, its image offered a star's protection to the slumbering soulless Demigods.

The knights of Sol fervently prayed for it to appear, hoping the dreadful event would call a spirit into the soulless demigod interred with their mausoleum. They planned to return the life of the demigod on behalf of Miquella the Kind. However, it never came to pass.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Black Knife Assassins are immune to all Status Effects except Frostbite.
- The sun is typically depicted with eight, ten, or sixteen points.
- The Eclipse emblem is available as a tattoo. It shows the color dripping from the sun in a way that resembles a sunflower.
- Castle Sol holds a Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left).
- "Drained of color" is also used to describe Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stones.
- The eclipsed sun is possibly synonymous with the polar star depicted on the Black Leather Shield.
- An eclipse likely occured in the past, possibly giving rise to the soulless king Ensha.
- The failure of the eclipse plan may have been a consequence of the Starscourge Conflict, when Starscourge Radahn halted the movement of the stars. It is also possible the revival was prevented by the Prince of Death setting the colorless eclipsed sun ablaze with his flames, spreading Death in the process.
 - Miquella finds a different way to summon the soul of Radahn into Mohg's body at the Gate of Divinity.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Fierce Demi-Humans** are enemies in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Demi-Humans are typically small in stature and bestial in appearance, often possessing fur, canine faces, and pointed ears. Although they are intelligent and capable of speech, as exemplified by Boc the Seamster, they are typically violent and brutish, particularly at night when their blood boils and they turn feral.

Demi-Humans wield a variety of weapons, such as falchions, daggers, and clubs. Those considered to be the toughest wield spiked clubs, which they believe to be a badge of honor.

Demi-Human society appears to be hierarchical, with the lesser Demi-Humans following much larger Demi-Human Chiefs. Demi-Humans lose hope if their leader dies, causing them to panic and stop attacking. At the top of the Demi-Human hierarchy are the Queens, who are capable of wielding rudimentary sorceries via their staves.

Despite their violent demeanour, Demi-Humans are capable of fostering diplomatic relations with humans, with Kenneth Haight building an alliance with a group of Demi-Humans in Fort Haight.

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.markdown: Larger, more bestial Demi-Humans that serve as leaders of their smaller brethren. Fierce Demi-Human walk on all four legs, and carry bloodstained daggers in each of their front paws. They strap large horns to their tattooed bodies.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- If one is killed, any nearby demi-humans are demoralized and stop fighting.
- The duo boss variant encountered in the Coastal Cave are both called Demi-Human Chief.
